Source contracts: src/agent_runtime/capability_scopes.py

src/agent_runtime/capability_scopes.py

Python · Tier A

Resolve and persist capability defaults and selection preferences across settings and conversations. CapabilityAuthority shares the Controller RAM hub or a standalone attached-SQL transaction, enforces optimistic revisions, and supports acceptance-time snapshots plus live dispatch restrictions. Defaults edits do not rewrite accepted runs; legacy conversation grants join the caller transaction while new resource grants have task-only ownership elsewhere.

Significant symbols

Symbol Line Documentation
CapabilityConflict 35 Signal a stale capability-policy revision or incompatible concurrent grant, allowing the API to require a fresh editor/approval decision instead of overwriting newer authority.
CapabilityAuthority 43 Coordinate global and conversation capability defaults, selection preferences and revision- checked grants across settings/chat stores. Shared-hub views support live Server transactions; attached SQLite databases support standalone stores. Acceptance snapshots and current dispatch restrictions have distinct roles.
CapabilityAuthority.connect 66 Yield a RAM settings view, optionally joined to the caller's transaction, or a managed SQLite settings connection with the chat database attached. Callers choose read/write transaction semantics; the managed SQL scope owns commit/rollback and closure.
CapabilityAuthority.read_in 78 Read one policy, selection preference and revision from the supplied cross-domain view or attached SQL connection. Preserve null inheritance versus an explicit default policy; a missing conversation identity yields an unset scope, but an unknown saved conversation raises.
CapabilityAuthority.resolve 143 Resolve complete policy snapshots and selection preferences independently in Prompt, Conversation, Global order. Validate selection against each effective ceiling and optionally return inherited editor views. Pending conversation defaults are accepted only for a new chat; scope_views=false also returns the compiled acceptance ceiling to avoid duplicate compilation.
CapabilityAuthority.normalize_selection 227 Canonicalize a supplied selection preference against registered identities while preserving None as inheritance. Effective-ceiling validation belongs to resolution or the write transaction.
CapabilityAuthority.normalize 233 Validate a supplied complete capability policy against the registry and return its JSON- compatible representation. Preserve None so removing an override does not become an explicit product-default selection.
CapabilityAuthority.set 243 Write capability defaults with revision checks in one settings transaction: use the shared authorization lock plus RAM atomic publication, or BEGIN IMMEDIATE for standalone SQLite. Existing accepted run snapshots are not rewritten by this defaults edit.
CapabilityAuthority.set_in 261 Normalize a policy and optional selection edit inside the caller's transaction, compare the expected revision and validate inherited selection against the resulting ceiling. UNCHANGED retains selection, None removes its override, and a successful write increments the scope revision. RAM and SQL branches persist the same settings/chat semantics.
CapabilityAuthority.dispatch_authority 356 For RAM-backed Server authority, resolve current applicable defaults while retaining an accepted explicit prompt policy, then reject tools or Shell executables now excluded. Opaque Shell syntax fails closed when exclusions apply. Return a PolicyBlock or None; standalone SQL returns None and accepted-ceiling checks remain with the execution path.
CapabilityAuthority.grant_in 445 Apply a legacy displayed conversation-capability grant within the native writer transaction. Compare both conversation and global revisions; tolerate only an already-converged effective policy/selection, otherwise raise conflict. Store the complete granted policy and selection atomically with the caller's authority decision. New task-resource grants use their separate task-only path.
